channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Trump says he would block US companies from building data centers overseas or impose a "tremendous tax" on them if they do (Julianna Bragg/Axios)
item.description: Former President Donald Trump proposed a policy aimed at anchoring AI infrastructure within the U.S., threatening to block American companies from constructing data centers abroad or imposing heavy taxes if they do so. This policy stance follows heightened voter concern over the environmental and financial impacts of domestic data center expansion, though the legal mechanism for implementing such taxes remains unclear given Congressional oversight.

item.title: Spying Suspect’s Chip Network Has Ties to Chinese Military Suppliers
item.description: Intelligence firm Strider Technologies identified that Alice Huang and her associates built a complex network utilizing $3.6 billion in Chinese government funding for data centers equipped with Nvidia AI chips. The investigation reveals that these entities maintain deep ties to Chinese military contractors and the Ministry of State Security, posing significant compliance risks regarding the diversion of restricted hardware into military research.

item.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
item.description: Nonprofit evaluation group METR has updated its time-horizon plot for AI capabilities, indicating that models show exponential growth in verifiable tasks like coding and mathematics, but lag in judgment-based tasks that lack automated verification. The report highlights the technological bottleneck in applying reinforcement learning to complex, open-ended research decisions, a capability critical for future autonomous R&D.

item.title: Top Republican Senator Says Lutnick Ignored His China Chip Warnings
item.description: Senator Tom Cotton, Chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of repeatedly ignoring warnings regarding the smuggling of AI chips to China. This criticism, following the Nvidia scandal, highlights growing congressional dissatisfaction with the Department of Commerce's regulatory oversight and enforcement efficacy.

item.title: Trump, Xi agreed humans must stay in charge of AI military decisions, Bessent says
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that humans must maintain control over military decisions involving artificial intelligence, prohibiting autonomous 'superintelligence' (SI) in major military actions, as confirmed by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The leaders also engaged in robust discussions regarding nuclear non-proliferation, trade policy, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, culminating in a joint declaration emphasizing that nuclear war must never be fought.

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’s most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world’s best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval already unleashed by OpenAI’s previous, often inelegant forays into the field. Alpöge’s solution has yet to be verified independently. Anthro

item.title: Linq, which offers texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, raised a $90M Series B led by a16z, following a $20M Series A in February (Harper Harwell/Birmingham Business Journal)
item.description: Linq, a provider of specialized communication infrastructure for AI agents, has secured $90 million in Series B funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This financing follows a $20 million Series A round in February, underscoring rapid capital deployment into the foundational connectivity layer of the AI agent ecosystem.

item.title: Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings shows AI-exposed roles in China fell 10 percentage points faster than others
item.description: of nearly 10 million job postings reveals that AI is significantly disrupting China's labor market, disproportionately affecting entry-level and creative roles. Vulnerable positions have seen a demand decline 10 percentage points sharper than non-impacted roles, with research from ShanghaiTech University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences confirming structural shifts including role consolidation and quiet staff reductions at major internet firms.

item.description: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician and employee at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, claimed on Friday to have proven the most famous problem in all of mathematics using an LLM. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a statement posted on his website. item.title: Anthropic Share Slump Nearly Erases IPO Pop As AI Trade Unravels
item.description: Anthropic PBC shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors' faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.

item.title: Apple joins the race for AI agents that control your device while raising new barriers for competitors
item.description: After Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google launched their own AI agents, Apple is now building one too - while making it harder for rivals to access its devices. According to a job listing, Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead the project as a rival to Muse, Dots, Duet, and Grok Bots. Privacy is expected to be central to the new agent, with permission models and sandboxing (protected test environments). According to Bloomberg, the agent could arrive as early as late next year, though it rem

item.title: Nvidia bets at least $500 million on Inception's diffusion models to strengthen its open-source Nemotron lineup
item.description: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million, including full-time integration of founders Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. Inception specializes in diffusion-based language models, such as Mercury 3, which refine responses globally rather than token-by-token. This acquisition is designed to enhance Nvidia's Nemotron open-source lineup and accelerate its physical simulation capabilities for robotics.

item.title: The week everything fell apart
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is embroiled in a growing scandal involving the alleged illegal smuggling of chips to China, fueling speculation regarding his potential exit. The core controversy centers on Nvidia’s compliance failures and internal control deficiencies amid increasingly stringent US export restrictions.

item.title: Anthropic raises $93.5 billion total as underwriters scoop up ‘greenshoe’ overallotment
item.description: AI firm Anthropic completed its historic IPO on Nasdaq, raising a total of $93.5 billion after underwriters exercised the greenshoe option for an additional $12.2 billion. Simultaneously, the company closed a $26 billion private placement involving major tech entities like AMD, Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia, bringing total gross proceeds to $119.5 billion.

item.title: Google's latest homepage update pushes its search engine further toward an AI answer engine
item.description: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar globally on its Desktop Search homepage, making AI search even easier to access. Announced on X by Google Search VP Robby Stein, the feature lets users easily find and reopen recent AI searches. Sitting on the left side of the AI Mode interface, it lets users start new threads, search existing ones, create notebooks, and open recent queries and settings. Stein said people are increasingly asking Google Search questions that a single query can't answer

item.title: Uber tests rides for kids as young as 10, with extra pay for drivers
item.description: Uber has launched the 'Uber Kids' pilot program in Austin, Nashville, and Madison, lowering the minimum ride-hailing age to 10. The service mandates parental onboarding, real-time video monitoring, PIN verification, and GPS-based off-course detection, while offering participating high-rated drivers a $7 premium per trip.

item.title: Threats, Insults, Settlements: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine
item.description: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly utilized aggressive management tactics, allegedly stating that as employees achieve financial independence due to the company's soaring market cap, humiliation becomes the primary tool to ensure continued high-intensity output. This governance philosophy has triggered internal concerns regarding organizational cohesion and long-term talent retention.

item.description: As Nvidia became wealthier and wealthier in recent years, Jensen Huang grew increasingly frustrated with his staff. He told groups of subordinates that they had become so rich that he couldn’t motivate them simply with money, according to three people who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential conversations. item.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
item.description: Meredith Whittaker, President of Signal, announced that integrated OS-level AI agents undermine app-level privacy. To mitigate this, Signal has disabled screenshot functionality on iOS and Android to prevent AI assistants from harvesting encrypted message data, while demanding that OS providers implement transparent technical controls for developer-side AI access management.

item.title: Muse Is Unleashing a World of Pettiness on Instagram
item.description: Meta's AI assistant Muse is being widely utilized by users to execute automated, bulk unfollow operations. The tool accurately identifies non-reciprocal followers and generates detailed category lists, while mitigating the risk of account suspension typically associated with third-party automated scripts.

item.title: China tightens approvals for offshore listings by red-chip firms, threatening Hong Kong IPO market: Reuters
item.description: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has informed law firms that red-chip companies established after the 2023 administrative measures for overseas securities offerings must relocate their place of incorporation to mainland China to receive approval for offshore listings. This policy signals a rigorous shift toward enforcing substantive domestic jurisdiction over overseas fundraising vehicles.

item.title: Ex-Alibaba Star’s AI Startup Doubles Valuation to $5 Billion
item.description: A generative AI startup founded by the former head of Alibaba Group's AI division has secured new funding, doubling its valuation to $5 billion within a few months. This capital injection underscores sustained investor confidence in the commercial viability of high-tier foundational model developers.

item.title: Signal to Restrict Screenshots to Block AI Agents, Urges Regulation on Apple, Google and Microsoft
item.description: Signal has introduced default screenshot restrictions to prevent OS-level AI agents, such as Apple Siri and Google Gemini, from scraping screen data and bypassing end-to-end encryption. The company stated that these agents pose a severe privacy threat by leveraging system-level permissions and has urged Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide more granular platform control tools.

item.title: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
item.description: Executives and core engineers in Silicon Valley are increasingly vigilant against corporate espionage facilitated through romantic relationships. Business intelligence and high-end matchmaking firms report a surge in demand for comprehensive background checks, non-disclosure agreements, and behavioral audits as standard defensive measures against the leakage of sensitive intellectual property.

item.title: SK Hynix to Convert Kioxia Bond and Become Top Shareholder
item.description: SK Hynix is considering converting its holdings in Kioxia convertible bonds into equity. This move is intended to solidify SK Hynix's strategic position as the largest shareholder of the Japanese NAND flash manufacturer amidst semiconductor market volatility and a cooling AI investment cycle.

item.title: SK Hynix To Be Kioxia S Top Shareholder After Bond Conversion
item.description: SK Hynix has announced plans to convert its holdings of Kioxia bonds into equity, resulting in a 14.1% stake and making the South Korean memory giant the largest shareholder in the Japanese storage manufacturer. This move is designed to deepen supply chain cooperation within the memory sector and strengthen strategic leverage in the NAND flash market.

item.title: Hermes Agent's Collective Wisdom feature turns one employee's AI trick into the whole team's skill
item.description: AI research lab Nous Research has launched an enterprise version of Hermes Agent, integrated into Microsoft Teams and secured within Azure Container Apps sandboxes. The new 'Collective Wisdom' feature enables employees to convert successful automated workflows into team-wide shared assets, while ensuring that internal operational data is excluded from third-party model training.

item.title: AI Threatens to Make China’s Jobs Slump Much Worse
item.description: Gartner projects a net gain of 1.7 million jobs by 2030, with 10.6 million created against 8.9 million lost globally. Chief forecaster John Lovelock notes that firms are transitioning from 'deferred hiring' to productive deployment, expecting a rebound in labor demand as AI systems move past the Trough of Disillusionment.

item.title: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, letting users easily find and resume recent AI searches (Barry Schwartz/Search Engine Roundtable)
item.description: Google has officially rolled out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, a strategic move by its search experience division to enhance continuity for users engaged in multi-turn AI queries. The feature is designed to shift search patterns from one-off interactions toward long-term engagement by providing a persistent hub for recent AI-generated tasks.
